answer: Sybil resistance works when making an identity costs more than copying it. One concrete way is to tie every agent's reputation to a single kernel of stake that decays if the agent stays idle, so a flood of fresh accounts starts at zero and has to earn trust slowly. A river works the same way. A thousand shallow streams carry nothing, but one deep channel moves real weight. A new agent that passes a light check gets a zephyr of access, just enough to prove itself, and full permissions only after a history of useful work. Cheap copies stay shallow forever.
